headline: High-risk shared-filesystem pair: mutual write access and default non-isolated execution create dangerous prompt-injection, data-leakage, and cascading-error pathways.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Cline and Open Interpreter both share state via filesystem, and Cline can use MCP plus browser/file inputs while Open Interpreter can read/write the whole local filesystem and clipboard. That creates a default pathway where one agent’s outputs can be treated as instructions by the other, with no provenance tracking or isolation shown.
conditions: IF either agent writes attacker-controlled text into a shared workspace file that the other later parses as instructions, injection is possible.
IF Cline uses MCP or browser-derived content as trusted input, Open Interpreter can be steered through shared files.
mitigations: Separate the agents into different workspaces.
Disable shared filesystem handoff between agents.
Require manual review of any file written by one agent before the other reads it.
Turn off MCP for Cline during cross-agent workflows.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging for inter-agent files.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Both agents have broad filesystem read/write and broad network egress, while Open Interpreter can access the entire user filesystem and clipboard. In a shared workspace, sensitive source code or local files touched by one agent can be exposed through the other’s outputs or outbound API calls; no default isolation is documented.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same workspace or user profile, files readable by one can be surfaced by the other.
IF either agent forwards file contents to its configured model provider, local data can leave the machine.
mitigations: Use separate OS users for each agent.
Keep sensitive files outside the shared workspace.
Disable clipboard-based transfer for Open Interpreter.
Review outbound model-provider settings before running either agent.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent filesystem ACLs.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents can execute shell commands, install packages, write files, and modify git state, and both share state via filesystem. Without locking or orchestration, concurrent edits can corrupt repositories, overwrite files, or create conflicting git history in default use.
conditions: IF both agents target the same git repository or directory, simultaneous writes can conflict.
IF one agent installs packages while the other edits the same environment, state drift can occur.
mitigations: Run only one agent per repository at a time.
Freeze package installation during shared work.
Use separate branches for each agent.
Add a manual checkpoint before git commits.
requires-engineering: add file and git locks in the orchestrator.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Cline can produce browser- and tool-derived outputs, and Open Interpreter can act on local files and shell commands. If Open Interpreter treats Cline’s output as authoritative, a mistaken or malicious intermediate result can cascade into destructive actions or incorrect commits without verification.
conditions: IF Open Interpreter consumes Cline-generated files or messages without verification, errors can propagate into actions.
IF Cline’s browser-derived content is used as factual input for shell actions, downstream mistakes can be executed.
mitigations: Require a human review step between agents.
Have Open Interpreter verify Cline outputs against primary sources.
Restrict Open Interpreter to read-only mode for handoff steps.
Use explicit schemas for handoff files.
requires-engineering: implement validation gates before action execution.

E_compliance.rationale: Open Interpreter exposes the entire user filesystem and clipboard, while Cline is workspace-scoped but still handles source code and browser screenshots. That creates a plausible retention/residency mismatch for sensitive local data, though the profiles do not show a specific regulated-data certification conflict.
conditions: IF regulated or sensitive data is present on the local machine, Open Interpreter can access more than Cline’s workspace scope.
IF either agent logs or retains copied content differently, policy mismatch can occur.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the shared machine.
Disable clipboard use for sensitive workflows.
Limit Open Interpreter to a dedicated directory.
Review retention settings for both agents.
requires-engineering: align logging and retention policies across tools.
